results.title: Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
**Yes—ResStock has a documented Maine wall type data problem, and no fix has been implemented.** Incorrect labeling in the underlying county tax assessor data produces an implausible distribution for Maine’s single-family detached homes: roughly 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete/CMU. The team believes all published ResStock datasets are affected. [Official issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team recommends:

- **For wall type or wall exterior finish distributions:** use nearby-state ResStock results, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For measures whose applicability depends on wall type:** reweight Maine results using nearby-state wall type distributions, or use nearby-state results directly.

This matters for measures restricted to wood-frame walls, which can appear applicable to too few Maine homes. The team currently does **not** expect significant effects on energy consumption, emissions, or energy bills, although its impact investigation remains incomplete. [Details and recommendations](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)
